title: Diel cycles in dissolved metal concentrations in streams: Occurrence and possible causes
water_body: Prickly Pear Creek (site 7), 26-28 Jun 2000

water_body: High Ore Creek (HO), 21-22 Aug 2010: DGT day deployment (09:00-16:45) vs night deployment (17:35-08:10)
measure: C_DGT (time-integrated labile, day vs night deployments)
location_in_paper: Fig. 5 (DGT bars/lines) with Fig. 2 (pH, T)
notes: C_DGT day = 1.429, night = 1.619, full 24-h = 1.453 ug/L (DGT lines in Fig. 5, read by line detection). authors: Brick CM, Moore JN
title: Diel variation of trace metals in the upper Clark Fork River, Montana
water_body: Clark Fork at Deer Lodge (site 3), 21-23 Jul 1994 (data of Brick & Moore 1996)
measure: dissolved, amplitude-based minimal slope log10(Cmax/Cmin)/(pH range)
location_in_paper: Nimick et al. 2003 Table 1 (maximum diel ranges of pH and dissolved metals; units ug/L)
notes: Amplitude-based: assumes concentration extremes coincide with pH extremes (sign from reported phase); extremes need not be simultaneous, so this is a minimal-information estimate; T co-varies (range given), so it is pH + T combined. Authors: pH-stat experiment with river sediment (oxic) released Mn and Zn only below pH 7.2-6.9, so pH-controlled desorption alone is NOT responsible; favour REDOX (reductive dissolution of Mn oxides at the sediment-water interface at night) and/or hyporheic influx tied to evapotranspiration.

authors: Nimick DA, Gammons CH, Cleasby TE, Madison JP, Skaar D, Brick CM
title: Diel cycles in dissolved metal concentrations in streams: Occurrence and possible causes
water_body: Coeur d'Alene River (site 1), 11-12 Sep 2001
measure: dissolved, amplitude-based minimal slope log10(Cmax/Cmin)/(pH range)
location_in_paper: Nimick et al. 2003 Table 1 (diel ranges) and text
notes: NULL/no diel cycle: no diel cycle with normal timing: subdued, lagged signal advected from South Fork (authors); pH range only 0.12 and T range 1.2 C. Upper bound on |slope| if all variation were pH-driven: 0.402. Authors: adsorption (pH- and temperature-dependent) is the only single mechanism explaining both As (anion, max late afternoon) and Cd/Mn/Zn (cations, max after sunrise); Mn redox and biological uptake also possible; Zn correlates more strongly with T (R2 0.83-0.91) than pH (0.62-0.80) but Fig. 10 amplitude analysis favours pH (p=0.003 vs 0.061). Cu inconsistent (colloidal). No cycle in acidic streams (pH<5.4).

authors: Brick CM, Moore JN
title: Diel variation of trace metals in the upper Clark Fork River, Montana
water_body: Upper Clark Fork River at Grant-Kohrs Ranch, Deer Lodge, Montana, 21-23 Jul 1994 (hourly, 46 h)
measure: dissolved (0.45-um): reported correlation with pH only
notes: Reported r2=0.83 (sign negative: concentrations 2-3x higher at night as pH falls); no lag between pH and dissolved Mn/Zn slope reversals on an hourly basis. Amplitude slope for the same data is given in the Clark Fork rows (Mn -0.87, Zn -0.95 per pH from Nimick 2003 Table 1). Dissolved Cu and Fe showed no diel variation. Lab pH-stat run (Fig. 5): dissolved Mn and Zn did not rise until pH fell to 7.2-6.9. Authors: pH-stat experiment with river sediment (oxic) released Mn and Zn only below pH 7.2-6.9, so pH-controlled desorption alone is NOT responsible; favour REDOX (reductive dissolution of Mn oxides at the sediment-water interface at night) and/or hyporheic influx tied to evapotranspiration.

authors: Nimick DA, Cleasby TE, McCleskey RB
title: Seasonality of diel cycles of dissolved trace-metal concentrations in a Rocky Mountain stream
water_body: Prickly Pear Creek at USGS 06061500, Montana: episode Jun 2000 (summer low flow)
measure: dissolved, amplitude-based minimal slope log10(Cmax/Cmin)/(pH range) (episode-average diel change)
location_in_paper: Fig. 6 (episode-average diel % change vs diel pH and T change; points extracted by blob detection, episode identity from Tables 2-3 and text)
notes: Episode-average diel change 446% (= (max-min)/min) with diel pH change 0.78 and diel T change 11.1 C; slope = -log10(1+change)/dpH. pH_min/pH_max not given per episode (seasonal pH: winter 7.86-8.24, snowmelt 7.65-8.24, summer 8.00-9.05). Across episodes authors fit delta Zn = -20.3 + 511 dpH (R2 0.72, p 0.02), delta Mn = -38.8 + 225 dpH (R2 0.91, p 0.05), delta As = 26.2 + 26.3 dpH (R2 0.29, p 0.46); relations with diel T change not significant (p 0.11-0.89). Authors: timing of minima/maxima consistent across seasons while flow timing varied, so geochemical not hydrological control; sorption best explains As; Mn/Zn may combine sorption, carbonate co-precipitation, Mn redox and uptake.
